newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Democrat MPs have expressed pessimism at the prime minister's decision to take personal charge of economic matters. They view Sunday's economic talks at Government House that preceded the announcement as an emergency meeting in which Amnuay Viravan, the Finance Minister and the government's top economic minister, was absent. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will urge the ruling military junta in Rangoon to certify the citizenship of Burmese working illegally in Thailand, a step that will facilitate the legalisation of their working status in the Kingdom. The proposal, seen as a marriage of convenience between Bangkok and its neighbour, was discussed yesterday during a meeting between government officials and the National Security Council, chaired by the prime minister. (THE NATION)

- A high-ranking official of the Science Ministry admits that campaigns have been mounted on the Internet against the ministry's three billion baht deal with Canada to buy a remote sensing satellite system. The sources has not disclosed the Internet address where the attacks are taking place, but says that critics claim the price is not worth the technology, which is not as good as that offered by a French company. (THE NATION)

- Electricity Generating Plc, the country's first private power producer, is conducting a feasibility study on the construction of a port for the transportation and storage of coal used in power production. The company says it will form a joint venture with major coal users for the proposed project. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Changes may be coming in the Board of Investment (BOI) zoning system to make the country more attrative to investors. The economic advisory team to the Prime Minister says that the current system needs an overhaul, and a BOI source acknowledges that changes are being considered. (BANGKOK POST)
